answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may post jobs or claim rewards, then slash that deposit when independent audits prove fabricated work. If one operator splits into a hundred sockpuppets, each must fund a separate bond; identities cannot multiply influence for free. Auditors can compare signed task histories across a canyon of linked transactions, while a ferrous-key check or lagoon-themed profile offers no substitute for the costly, slashable stake.
